title: “I AM JOSEPH.”
paragraphs: “I AM JOSEPH.”
The room froze.

The most powerful man in Egypt…
just spoke the name they buried.
The brothers felt the blood drain from their faces.
Because they remembered.

The pit.
The rope.
The silver coins.
The screams of a 17-year-old boy they sold like livestock.
And now… that boy stood before them wearing the authority of a kingdom.
Silence.

Heavy.
Terrifying.
Because this was the moment judgment could fall.
But Joseph didn’t call the guards.
He wept.
Loud enough that the palace heard it.
“I am Joseph. Is my father still alive?” — Genesis 45:3
The brothers couldn’t answer.
Not because they forgot how to speak.
Because guilt was choking them.
They expected revenge.
Joseph gave them revelation.
“Do not be distressed or angry with yourselves for selling me here, because it was to save lives that God sent me ahead of you.” — Genesis 45:5
Pause there.
They sold him.
God sent him.

Same event.
Different author.

What looked like betrayal…
was actually God positioning a rescuer.

The pit led to Potiphar.
The prison led to the palace.
The suffering led to salvation.
Joseph wasn’t just surviving.
He was being prepared to feed nations during famine.
Even the brothers who betrayed him.
This is the mystery of providence:
Humans meant evil.
God meant rescue.
But the story doesn’t stop with Joseph.
Joseph is a shadow.
Because centuries later, another Son would be betrayed by His own.
Sold for silver.
Rejected by His brothers.
Crucified between criminals.
Yet through that betrayal…
God saved the world.
Jesus didn’t just forgive His betrayers.
He became the bread that feeds them.
Joseph saved people from famine.
Christ saves us from sin and eternal death.
That’s the Gospel hidden in Genesis.
Your worst chapters are not the end of the story.

The pit you hate…
might be the place God begins your rescue.

The betrayal that broke you…
might be the road God uses to save someone else.
Because God still writes redemption into human mess.
He still turns betrayal into rescue.
And if Joseph could forgive the men who sold him…
How much more does Jesus forgive those who come to Him?
Today the invitation still stands.
Come home.
Come honest.
Come broken if you must.
Grace is waiting.
Because God turned betrayal into rescue.
And Jesus still receives sinners.
We tell the stories that shame tried to erase.
